name: Question 1
problem:
Consider a function $q(t)$ such that its Laplace transform is $L{q(t)}=Q(s)$ for $s>{s}_{0}.$ Suppose we wish to find $L{{e}^{9t}q(t)}.$ Select the correct options in the reasoning below.By definition of the Laplace transform, we can write 

$$
\begin{aligned}L{{e}^{9t}q(t)} & ={\int }_{0}^{\infty }{{field-1}}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\infty }{{field-2}}\,q(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={{field-3}}\,\text{for}\,{{field-4}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 1

Consider a function q(t) such that its Laplace transform is L{q(t)}=Q(s) for s>s0. Suppose we wish to find L{e9tq(t)}. Select the correct options in the reasoning below.By definition of the Laplace transform, we can write

 
est⋅e−9tq(t)
e−st⋅e9tq(t)
e−st⋅e−9tq(t)
est⋅e9tq(t)
 
e−(s−9)t
e(s+9)t
e(s−9)t
e−(s+9)t
 
Q(s−9)
Q(s)
Q(s+9)
 
s>s0−9
s>s0+9
s>s0
L{e9tq(t)}=∫0∞{(est⋅e−9tq(t))(S0)}dt=∫0∞{(e−(s−9)t)(S1)}q(t)dt={(Q(s−9))(S2)}for{(s>s0−9)(S3)}.
